recognize_zh: 皮膚切片免疫染色中，真皮血管周圍成團的中型異型淋巴球呈強陽性，且有陽性細胞散入表皮基底層（epidermotropism），符合 T 細胞淋巴瘤侵犯皮膚；需配合 HTLV-1 血清學才能歸為 ATLL。
features: Dermal perivascular aggregates of medium-sized lymphoid cells with strong membranous/cytoplasmic brown immunoreactivity
Positive cells have irregular, somewhat enlarged nuclei compared with background stromal cells
Scattered positive cells within the basal layer of the epidermis and hair follicle epithelium (epidermotropism/folliculotropism)
Scattered single positive cells in the intervening dermis
Fibroblasts, endothelium and keratinocytes are negative (internal negative control)
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain of a skin biopsy (specific marker not indicated in the image) highlights perivascular dermal aggregates of atypical medium-sized lymphoid cells with strong membranous and cytoplasmic staining. Positive cells also infiltrate the basal epidermis and follicular epithelium as single cells. Keratinocytes and stromal cells are negative. The staining pattern supports a cutaneous T-cell infiltrate; in the appropriate context (HTLV-1 seropositivity, CD4+/CD25+ phenotype), findings are consistent with cutaneous involvement by adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

ddx.vs: MF shows a similar epidermotropic CD4+ infiltrate, so separation relies on HTLV-1 serology/monoclonal integration and the strong, diffuse CD25 expression typical of ATLL.
Lymphomatoid papulosis/cutaneous ALCL show large anaplastic cells with uniform strong CD30, whereas this infiltrate is composed of medium-sized cells.
Reactive infiltrates consist of small, non-atypical mixed T cells without clonal markers or HTLV-1 association.
